# Start-ZbxActiveAgent

## SYNOPSIS

Starts an active agent as a session: it asks its servers which items to collect, answers the built-in keys, and pushes agent data until stopped.

## SYNTAX

```
Start-ZbxActiveAgent [-Name] <string> [[-HostName] <string>] [-Server] <string> [-HostMetadata <string>] [-RefreshInterval <TimeSpan>] [-HeartbeatInterval <TimeSpan>] [-Tls <ZabbixTlsMode>] [-PassThru] [-KeyRule <string[]>] [-NoBundledItems] [-Plugin <string[]>] [-PluginPath <string>] [-PluginSetting <Hashtable>] [-PskIdentity <string>] [-Psk <SecureString>] [-Certificate <string>] [-CertificateKey <string>] [-CertificateAuthority <string>] [-CertificateRevocationList <string>] [-ServerIssuer <string>] [-ServerSubject <string>] [-WhatIf] [-Confirm] [<CommonParameters>]
```

## DESCRIPTION

The session is kept in this runspace under -Name (see Get-ZbxActiveAgentStatus, Stop-ZbxActiveAgent); pass -PassThru to also write it. Give -PskIdentity and -Psk to connect with a pre-shared key, or -Certificate, -CertificateKey and -CertificateAuthority to connect with certificates (Zabbix's TLSConnect, -Tls, chooses when both are given).

## EXAMPLES

### Example 1: Start an active agent for a host

```powershell
Start-ZbxActiveAgent -Name 'web-agent' -Hostname 'web-01' -Server 'zabbix.example:10051'
Get-ZbxActiveAgentStatus -Name 'web-agent' | Select-Object Name, Kind, Started
Stop-ZbxActiveAgent -Name 'web-agent'
```

The agent asks the server's trapper which active items (type ZabbixActive) host web-01 has, answers the built-in keys (agent.ping, agent.version, agent.hostname, system.uname, and Zabbix's own keys such as vfs.fs.size and proc.num) and pushes the values, in the background of this runspace, until Stop-ZbxActiveAgent or the runspace closes. -Name is only the session's local name; -KeyRule limits the keys it answers, as on Start-ZbxPassiveAgent.

### Example 2: Watch the values arrive on the server

```powershell
Start-ZbxActiveAgent -Name 'web-agent' -Hostname 'web-01' -Server 'zabbix.example:10051'
Start-Sleep -Seconds 10
Get-ZbxItem -Host 'web-01' | Where-Object Type -eq 'ZabbixActive' | Select-Object Key, LastValue
Stop-ZbxActiveAgent -Name 'web-agent'
```

The agent re-asks for its items every -RefreshInterval (5 seconds by default) and sends each value when the item's own interval is due; the server then shows it as the item's LastValue.

### Example 3: Start an agent with host metadata and its own cadence

```powershell
Start-ZbxActiveAgent -Name 'web-agent' -Hostname 'web-01' -Server 'zabbix.example:10051' -HostMetadata 'Linux web' `
    -RefreshInterval '30s' -HeartbeatInterval '2m' -PassThru |
    Select-Object Name, Kind, Started
Stop-ZbxActiveAgent -Name 'web-agent'
```

-HostMetadata is what auto-registration actions filter on; -RefreshInterval and -HeartbeatInterval take Zabbix's time suffixes ('30s', '2m'), seconds or a time span. -PassThru writes the session. -Server is Zabbix's ServerActive text: 'a;b' is one HA cluster, tried in turn; 'a,b' is two independent destinations, each sent every value. Quote it: PowerShell ends a command at a bare ';'.

### Example 4: Run an agent for the length of a script

```powershell
Start-ZbxActiveAgent -Name 'web-agent' -Hostname 'web-01' -Server 'zabbix.example:10051'
try {
    Start-Sleep -Seconds 6
    $status = (Get-ZbxActiveAgentStatus -Name 'web-agent').AgentStatus
    'Delivered {0} value(s), {1} rejected' -f $status.Delivered, $status.Rejected
}
finally {
    Stop-ZbxActiveAgent -Name 'web-agent'
}
```

A script that pushes agent data while it does its own work, and always stops the agent, even on failure.

## PARAMETERS

### -Server

Where the agent sends, as Zabbix's ServerActive spells it: host or host:port (port 10051 when omitted; an IPv6 address with a port is bracketed, [::1]:10051). In one string, ; separates the nodes of one HA cluster, tried in order on failover ('zbx1;zbx2'), and , separates independent destinations, each sent every value ('zbx-a,zbx-b'); quote the text, because PowerShell reads a bare ; as the end of the command. A list (-Server zbx1, zbx2) is the nodes of one HA cluster, as every other -Server reads it.

### -KeyRule

Which keys the agent answers, as lines of Zabbix's agent configuration, tried in order, the first that matches deciding: 'AllowKey=vfs.file.*[*]', 'DenyKey=*'. In a pattern * matches any characters, in the name or in a parameter. Without it the agent answers every key but system.run, as Zabbix's agents do. A denied key is answered as one nobody answers.

Leaves out the bundled items, Zabbix's own system, process, file, network and web keys: the session answers the four keys every agent answers, its scriptblock handlers and its plugins only.

### -Plugin

Plugins to load into the agent, by name: each a folder under -PluginPath holding a plugin's dotnet publish output, whose item keys the agent then answers beside the built-in keys and the session's scriptblock handlers. A plugin that cannot be loaded fails the start, and a plugin whose files other accounts can write is refused on Linux and macOS.
